subject: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test — allowlist and test-account plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test — allowlist and test-account plan

Thanks again for the demo this morning, Olivia — great discussion. Per our call I wanted to capture the requirements we agreed and propose the next steps for the customer-led load test so your network and devops teams can review.

High-level SLOs / targets you mentioned
- Latency: p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 200 ms (goal for production)
- Throughput: sustained 300–400 req/s for the targeted endpoint set
- Concurrency: tests should validate 50 -> 150 concurrent users/threads (ramped)
- Streaming: some endpoints rely on chunked/streaming responses — please confirm whether you need server-sent events (SSE) style streaming or chunked transfer (we support both; k6 config attached)

Proposed test plan (attached: fastretail_k6_plan_v1.yaml)
1) Smoke (5–10 m): validate auth and endpoints with single-threaded k6 job
2) Ramp (20–30 m): increase from 5 -> 150 concurrent VUs to hit target throughput
3) Soak (60 m): hold near expected sustained load (300 req/s) to check stability and memory/latency drift
4) Spike test (10 m): short high-concurrency bursts to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies

What we need from FastRetail to run the above (next steps)
- IP allowlist: please confirm the network team can allow our load generator ranges (we list ranges below) or provide the FastRetail egress IP ranges that will run the tests (if you run k6 from your env)
- Test account: we will provision a temporary test API key scoped to the test endpoints (instructions attached) — confirm who should receive the key
- Test window: propose Tue Feb 24, 01:00–04:00 UTC (low-traffic window). If that conflicts, share alternatives.

Temporary test constraints (for safety)
- Test API key will be limited to model redwood-small-v2 and to 2048 tokens/request; will be rate-limited to prevent noisy neighbor effects
- We recommend disabling production side-effects (billing triggers, writes to production DB) — please confirm staging endpoints where applicable

Action items
- Olivia / DevOps: confirm allowlist IPs and preferred test window
- Connor / Redwood: create test account and share key and k6 script link
- Dylan / Redwood: provide allowlist CSV and step-by-step test account instructions

Attachments: [Attachment: fastretail_k6_plan_v1.yaml (text/yaml)]

Thanks — I'll schedule the ticket in HubSpot once you confirm the window.

—
Connor O'Brien

2) We prefer to run k6 from our env (we have runners in us-east-1) — is the k6 plan you attached runnable as-is from our side? Any special headers / auth flow we should include?

Hi Olivia — copying the specific details your firewall will need. We can run the k6 scripts from our runners or you can execute them from your us-east-1 runners. Both are supported; running from your side avoids egress changes.

IP ranges for Redwood-managed k6 runners (if you choose us to execute):
- 34.85.10.0/24
- 35.200.20.0/24
Note: testers will use standard HTTPS (443) and ephemeral outbound ports for TLS handshakes.

I've provisioned a temporary test API key that's scoped to staging endpoints and model redwood-small-v2. Key details and usage steps are in the attached PDF. Highlights:
- TTL: 72 hours from issuance
- Rate limit on key: 500 requests/sec aggregated across all runners (we can lift this to 1k/s for scheduled windows if you confirm)
- Token limits: 2k tokens per request enforced at the gateway

Attached: redwood-test-account-instructions.pdf, allowlist_IPs.csv (CSV includes IPs plus ASN notes).

Guidance for k6 / Locust scripts
- The attached YAML is configured for the ramp/soak/spike phases. If you want Locust I'll share a converted script — we maintain both variants in our repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadtests/fastretail/k6-scripts/tree/main
- For streaming endpoints, ensure the k6 websocket plugin or chunked transfer handling is enabled (example in the YAML).

Suggested test cadence (if you run from your env)
1) Smoke: run 15 m to validate auth and session handling
2) Ramp: 30–45 m to climb to 150 concurrent users
3) Soak: 60 m at target throughput
4) Ramp down and collect p95/p99 histograms and heap summaries

If you want Redwood to run the tests, reply and we'll provide a signed AUP + IP allowlist ticket for your network team.
